newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends mixed, nearbys down on weak cash.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends mixed, nearbys down on weak cash.

text.p: CBOT rice futures closed mixed on Monday with nearbys down on weak cash demand but new crop months were steady to higher as concerns mounted that heavy rains in Texas would delay plantings, traders said.
"We're just struggling with a nominal cash market," a floor trader said.
"The U.S. rice market has got a weather problem," he added. "We've gone from being wet in Texas to being flooded and the extended forecasts are still calling for more rain."
Trade sources said it would be at least a week, possibly two weeks before fields dried out enough for planting.
Export demand was quiet but some floor sources noted persistent rumors Costa Rica and Colombia were looking to buy U.S. supplies.
Rice ended three cents per cwt lower to two cents higher with May unchanged at $11.68.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 400 lots, compared with Friday's actual volume of 576 lots.
